posts.description:
Another week and another update on a fast startup life:
We hosted our first dinner in San Francisco! On AI adoption!
Leaders from Lyft, TaskRabbit, Freshworks, Abridge and others joined!

So what did we hear?

1. Most leaders come up with AI workflows by experimenting themselves! They think ‘imagination’ is the key skill.

2. Leaders can be far away from the ‘day to day work’ which makes it hard for them to identify and build useful AI workflows.

3. Trainings are old fashioned, and it is not working for AI.

4. There is a serious expectation for the new hires to be AI native from day one! Not an easy task to fulfill!

5. Being ‘mostly accurate’ for an AI tool is not enough for regulated industries which really hinders the adoption.

6. And unfortunately… the fear of being left behind and be replaced by AI... 

I picked a Turkish restaurant, so there was plenty of cultural chat among the AI chat :)

Well, what are your takes on these?

How do you come up with AI workflows for your team? Do you ask Claude?

If you are looking for a job, how do you feel about the ‘AI native’ request?…

What do you think is the best way to train on AI?

And… if you are interested joining the next AI adoption dinner, we’re currently planning for big cities in the US, please DM me!

--
Thank you for your time and presense! Alisa Liebowitz Chris Lambert Kanishka Thakur Kalia Waits-Smith ⛸️ Dilek Barlow Gurtej Gill Bethel Zelalem, MSOD, PMP Kevin Law Sameer Shariff
